answer: Sealed-storage proofs make every agent key pay in live disk. Each key must hold its own 64 GB copy of ledger history, encoded by a slow seal tied to its address, so no two keys share a block. A new key faces a high tide of audits, 10 a day, which ebbs to 2 a day after 30 clean days. Each audit names a random 4 KB slice, picked by a yarrow draw cast from the latest block hash, and must be answered within 2 seconds, too fast to re-seal. A nebula of 1,000 fake keys needs 64 TB online, and 3 missed audits evict a key.
